title: IELTS Academic 20 - Listening Test 4 - Part 3
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 3

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

15:54ANNOUNCER: Part 3. You will hear two education students discussing an assignment on teaching handwriting to children.
16:03ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 24.
16:33ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 24.
16:41MAN: How are you getting on with the assignment on handwriting?
16:45WOMAN: Not too bad. You know, I hadn't realised that children benefit in so many ways from learning to write... And all the evidence suggests children should learn to write by hand before they learn to type. Not least because it helps their memory.
17:12MAN: That's right. The physical act of writing helps children to remember letters. That seems pretty obvious when you think about it. What's less obvious is how it helps develop their concentration. They have to sit still and focus on one thing. WOMAN: Yeah. That aspect of handwriting had never occurred to me before. MAN: Hmm, same here.
17:35MAN: I'm not sure I understand how it improves children's imagination though. Well, there was that study which showed that primary age children generated more ideas... I would have guessed that would be the case.
17:53WOMAN: I'd never associated spatial awareness with handwriting either. I thought spatial awareness was more to do with knowing where you are in relation to objects or other people. MAN: I thought that too. But good spatial awareness is essential for writing because you have to space words correctly.
18:19MAN: Handwriting is so much harder for children with dyspraxia who have problems coordinating movement. It's good there are lots of things you can do in the classroom to help them. They need so much more support with letter formation. You need to play lots of games to help them distinguish letter shapes. It takes a lot of patience.
18:40WOMAN: I like the idea of using one of those pens that lights up if you press too hard. That seems like a really simple solution. MAN: Yes, absolutely.
18:49MAN: I'm not sure there's much you can do about children with dyspraxia writing very slowly. It's more important to focus on accuracy and as they get more confident, I think they eventually speed up.
19:03WOMAN: One quite simple thing you can do is to use grid paper. So they write each letter in a box and that trains them to space the letters correctly. MAN: Indeed, that's more important for legibility than trying to get them to write in a straight line.
19:22ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 25 to 30.
20:19ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 25 to 30.
20:26MAN: For some children it might be better to teach them to write on a laptop rather than by hand. Like children with dyslexia. They often really struggle with handwriting and some just give up.
20:39WOMAN: Yeah, it's not as frustrating for them if they get things wrong. On a keyboard they can be more willing to have a go. But I read that developing fluency isn't any faster.
20:53MAN: Did you read that article on the benefits of teaching print rather than cursive handwriting, where the letters are joined up?
21:02WOMAN: Well, in the past, cursive writing was certainly considered more stylish and educated, but not anymore. Teachers' attitudes have changed because it's been proved that cursive is more difficult to learn, especially for children with learning difficulties who find joining up letters really challenging.
21:23WOMAN: I was always worried that my poor handwriting affected my exam results and now research shows that I was right to worry. I'm sure a lot of students think it's unfair that they're being judged on their handwriting, not just their knowledge. Marks are definitely affected if examiners can't read the script. That's why it's always been so important to teach children to write legibly.
21:49WOMAN: Do you think the role of handwriting will change in the future?
21:53MAN: I can't see that changing much. Touch typing still isn't taught in most schools, which is a shame. But maybe that won't be necessary in the future, because people will also be able to write by hand on digital devices. Anyway, teachers understand the value of handwriting. It's a basic life skill.
22:15WOMAN: However, the fact is that people are writing by hand less and less and relying on digital devices. That does cause some problems. My mum is shocked by my awful spelling and the fact that my punctuation is really inconsistent.
22:45MAN: Personally, I miss writing by hand. I hardly ever write anything now. I remember my grandparents had such beautiful handwriting... It's a shame. WOMAN: I know. I feel the same way. I used to write a diary by hand and now I do that digitally.
23:19ANNOUNCER: That is the end of Part 3. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to Part 3.

groups.title: Questions 21 and 22
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
Which TWO benefits for children of learning to write did both students find surprising?
options: A. improved fine motor skills
B. improved memory
C. improved concentration
D. improved imagination
E. improved spatial awareness

groups.title: Questions 23 and 24
groups.instructions:
Choose TWO letters, A–E.
For children with dyspraxia, which TWO problems with handwriting do the students think are easiest to correct?
options: A. not spacing letters correctly
B. not writing in a straight line
C. applying too much pressure when writing
D. confusing letter shapes
E. writing very slowly

q21.text: Surprising benefits of learning to write (First benefit)

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C & E
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'What's less obvious is how it helps develop their concentration... never occurred to me before. Hmm, same here' (= C: improved concentration).
• 'I'd never associated spatial awareness with handwriting either... I thought that too' (= E: improved spatial awareness).

q22.text: Surprising benefits of learning to write (Second benefit)

steps: • Đáp án đúng: E & C

• Phân tích bẫy: Cải thiện trí nhớ (memory) thì rõ ràng quá rồi ('pretty obvious' - loại B). Trí tưởng tượng (imagination) thì hai người nói 'would have guessed that would be the case' (đã đoán trước như vậy - loại D).

q23.text: Easiest problems to correct in dyspraxia (First problem)

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C & A
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'using one of those pens that lights up if you press too hard. That seems like a really simple solution' (= C: applying too much pressure).

q24.text: Easiest problems to correct in dyspraxia (Second problem)

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A & C

• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'use grid paper... trains them to space the letters correctly. Indeed, that's more important for legibility than trying to get them to write in a straight line' (= A: not spacing letters correctly).

q25.text: What does the woman say about using laptops to teach writing to children with dyslexia?
options: A. Children often lack motivation to learn that way.
B. Children become fluent relatively quickly.
C. Children react more positively if they make a mistake.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (Children react more positively if they make a mistake)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'it's not as frustrating for them if they get things wrong. On a keyboard they can be more willing to have a go.'
• Phân tích bẫy: Về độ trôi chảy, bài nói 'developing fluency isn't any faster' nên loại B.

q26.text: When discussing whether to teach cursive or print writing, the woman thinks that
options: A. Cursive writing disadvantages a certain group of children.
B. Print writing is associated with lower academic performance.
C. Most teachers in the UK prefer a traditional approach to handwriting.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (Cursive writing disadvantages a certain group of children)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'cursive is more difficult to learn, especially for children with learning difficulties who find joining up letters really challenging.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'children with learning difficulties' = a certain group of children.

q27.text: According to the students, what impact does poor handwriting have on exam performance?
options: A. There is evidence to suggest grades are affected by poor handwriting.
B. Neat handwriting is less important now than it used to be.
C. Candidates write more slowly and produce shorter answers.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (There is evidence to suggest grades are affected by poor handwriting)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'now research shows that I was right to worry... Marks are definitely affected if examiners can't read the script.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'Marks are definitely affected' = grades are affected.

q28.text: What prediction does the man make about the future of handwriting?
options: A. Touch typing will be taught before writing by hand.
B. Children will continue to learn to write by hand.
C. People will dislike handwriting on digital devices.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (Children will continue to learn to write by hand)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'I can't see that changing much... teachers understand the value of handwriting. It's a basic life skill.'

q29.text: The woman is concerned that relying on digital devices has made it difficult for her to
options: A. take detailed notes.
B. spell and punctuate.
C. read old documents.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (spell and punctuate)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'my mum is shocked by my awful spelling and the fact that my punctuation is really inconsistent.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'awful spelling... punctuation is really inconsistent'.

q30.text: How do the students feel about their own handwriting?
options: A. concerned they are unable to write quickly
B. embarrassed by comments made about it
C. regretful that they have lost the habit

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (regretful that they have lost the habit)

• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'Personally, I miss writing by hand. I hardly ever write anything now... It's a shame. WOMAN: I know. I feel the same way. I used to write a diary by hand and now I do that digitally.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'miss writing by hand / It's a shame' = regretful that they have lost the habit.
